From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Eva Martinez <eva@clearledger.com>; Sam Richards <sam.richards@clearledger.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: ClearLedger integration: auth model, routing & SDK handoff (post-demo)

Hi Eva / Sam —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we discussed and concrete next steps so we don’t lose momentum: a short technical checklist, recommended auth approaches, and a proposed sandbox timeline.

1) What you asked us to validate
- Embeddings + reranker pipeline for search ranking and recommendation flows
- Tool/structured output support for transaction enrichment (webhook/tool call chaining)
- Secure token management with rotation & audit for third-party access

2) Recommended auth approach (short summary)
- For integration with ClearLedger apps we recommend a service-account + short-lived JWT flow as the primary pattern: Redwood issues long-lived service credentials that exchange for 15m JWTs scoped to specific routes (embed, rerank, tool-call). This keeps your user-facing secrets off devices and gives clear audit windows.
- Fallback option: scoped API keys with enforced per-route quotas and automatic rotation (useful for quick POC).
- For procurement/compliance, we can wire the credential material into your KMS / Vault and support HSM-backed signing for JWTs.

3) Routing & model selection notes
- Embeddings: suggest embed-compact-v2 for production (good density/latency); fall back to embed-compact-v1-quant for batch re-index jobs to save cost.
- Reranker: route rerank requests to rerank-v1 (GPU optimized). If latency SLOs are strict, enable prefix caching for top-k candidates and keep rerank calls to the hot path only.
- Tool calling/structured outputs: promote typed outputs (JSON schema) from the start — Redwood will enforce schema validation at the SDK layer so service calls downstream are deterministic.

4) Security + key rotation cadence
- Recommended rotation cadence: service credentials rotated every 90 days, JWTs short-lived (15m), and a pipeline to rotate signing keys in KMS every 30 days for compliance-sensitive environments.
- We provide a rotation webhook so your infra can automatically request new signed JWTs; detailed automation templates attached.

5) Sandbox and next steps (mutual action plan)
- Redwood: provision sandbox project, sample integration playbook, and a pre-seeded embedding index (ETA: 48 hours) — Ben
- ClearLedger: provide a test account, sample data for 10k docs, and a security contact for SOC2 evidence (ETA: 3 business days) — Eva / Sam
- Joint: 45-minute SDK walk-through + auth exchange demo next Wed 11/03 10:00 PT — calendar invite pending.

Attachments: sample-integration-playbook.md (integration steps), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (high-level security artifacts).

If that looks right I’ll schedule the SDK demo and loop in our infra engineer to start the JWT keyflow setup.

Thanks,
Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: ClearLedger integration: auth model, routing & SDK handoff (post-demo)

Thanks Ben — that all tracks and the approach sounds promising. A few clarifying questions before we jump into the SDK session: 

1) On service accounts: do you expect ClearLedger to host the private key material, or will Redwood sign JWTs for us? We have a Vault-backed key policy and prefer to keep signing in-house if feasible.

2) Rotation automation: can the rotation webhook you mentioned integrate with our CI (we use GitHub Actions + Vault)? Any sample workflow would help.

3) Reranker latency: what latency should we budget for per-request for rerank-v1 at 100 qps with a top-k=50 rerank? We need to validate SLAs with product.

Finally, procurement asked for an abbreviated SOW and an expected monthly run-rate estimate for the proposed config (embed-compact-v2 + rerank-v1 with 2x reserved capacity). Can you loop in your sales ops for numbers?

Appreciate it — we’ll confirm the test data export by EOD.

— Eva
Head of Integrations
ClearLedger

Subject: Re: ClearLedger integration: auth model, routing & SDK handoff (post-demo)

Eva — great questions. Short answers + specific artifacts we’ll bring to the SDK demo: 

1) Signing model (Vault vs Redwood)- We can support both:
  - Option A (preferred for ClearLedger compliance): you generate and host the signing key in Vault/HSM. Redwood will accept signed JWTs and validate via a JWKS endpoint you publish. This keeps signing in your control.
  - Option B (managed): Redwood hosts the signing key in our HSM and issues signed JWTs via an authenticated exchange. We provide full audit logs and key rotation reports.

2) Rotation + CI integration- We have a GitHub Actions example that calls the rotation webhook to request a new short-lived credential and writes the credential to Vault using the Vault API. We’ll paste the workflow in the demo and provide a runnable template.

3) Reranker latency (budget)- At 100 qps with top-k=50: expect median p95 around 120-180ms on rerank-v1 with dedicated capacity; p99 occasionally spikes if cold KV-cache misses occur. Enabling per-request prefix caching (store top-50 candidate embeddings) typically drops p95 ~30–40ms. We’ll include a perf microbenchmark in the sandbox.

4) Commercial estimate and SOW- Looping in Vanessa (cc) to provide ballpark pricing and an SOW template. Vanessa — can you provide a 2x reserved capacity estimate and an SOW draft we can share with ClearLedger procurement?

Planned deliverables for the SDK session (Wed 11/03):
- Live auth exchange demo (Vault + managed flow) — Ben
- SDK install, example call patterns for embeddings and rerank (Node + Python) — Marissa
- Preliminary pricing + SOW template — Vanessa

If you’re happy with that, I’ll lock the calendar and provision the sandbox project.

Thanks,
Ben
